title: (Re-issue of 20261025T1531-c17-review-evoloop with seed results reworded; the build's failure regex read 'neutral does not' as a failed seed) Evoloop review with the H gate control on 10 new seeds: a planted side-4 loop sweeps side-11 residents on 7/9 usable seeds vs 2/9 for the matched side-11 plant (sign test p=0.03); D replicates on fresh seeds 4 and 5 (gen 28)
summary: Labkit re-run of the claimed world on fresh seeds 4 and 5 with the claim's pack settings (300^2, 20k steps, spf 100, lineage K=3): 247 and 255 persistent splits, max generation 28, merge/split 0.38, matching the claim's 218-224 and 27-28. Gate control for H: c16's invasion design (invade.py, unchanged) on 10 new seeds, 40-49. The claim's world runs to t=20000, then the same seed-chosen 40x40 patch is cleared in both arms and one side-4 loop (invader) or one side-11 loop (neutral, the residents' kind) is planted with the same orientation; hole sides are counted every 1000 steps for 40k steps. Seed 42 had already swept spontaneously to side 4 before the plant and is excluded; in both of its arms side 3 then replaces side 4. On the 9 usable seeds, side 4 reaches a majority in the invader arm on 7, 3000-5000 steps after planting (one at 20000), and in the neutral arm on 2 (5000 and 39000 steps, from spontaneous mutants). 5 seeds sweep only in the invader arm and none only in the neutral arm (one-sided sign test p=0.031). The 2 invader failures (seeds 48, 49) are early losses of the single planted loop. Spontaneous small-kind sweeps happen in the unplanted world too: seed 42 before t=20000, and seeds 40 and 46 in the neutral arm. So variation arises during the run and the small kind is favoured.

verdicts.limitation: The neutral arm is a matched plant of the residents' kind, not an identical-event twin of spontaneous mutations; the test shows that side 4 is favoured once present, not that every claimed sweep was selection. I did not re-run the 200k-step tracker on a fresh seed or check the claim's seed-2 track. Kind conversions of living loops were taken from the claim's demography.json, not re-measured. S fails (planted founders). Evoloop's drift toward small loops is known from Sayama (1999), so novelty is low.
